title: Safeguards to Ensure Religious Teachers Accredited under Asatizah Recognition Scheme Do Not Hold Radical Views
what_it_is: Safeguards to Ensure Religious Teachers Accredited under Asatizah Recognition Scheme Do Not Hold Radical Views

sections.label: Asatizah Recognition Scheme safeguards
sections.summary: Question asks about safeguards against radical views, periodic review of accreditation, and independent oversight of the Asatizah Recognition Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) what safeguards are in place to ensure that the religious teachers who are accredited under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) do not hold radical views; (b) whether there are mechanisms to periodically review and renew the ARS accreditation; and (c) whether there is an independent oversight body to review the ARS accreditation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This includes not encouraging extremism or violence, denigrating other racial and religious groups, committing ethical misconduct and promoting segregationist practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Asatizah Recognition Board (ARB) oversees the ARS and is supported by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In the case of Mr Murad Mohd Said, who was placed on a Restriction Order in December 2018, his ARS-recognition was cancelled in May 2018, after he contravened the ARS Code of Ethics.

sections.label: ARS registration processes and renewal
sections.summary: Processes include observation periods, interviews, three-yearly renewal, regular training, periodic suitability review, and cancellation for Code of Ethics breaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Processes have been put in place to ensure that our asatizahs registered with ARS can perform the role that the community entrusts them to do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: These processes include instituting provisional periods of observation and requiring additional interviews when deemed necessary by ARB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Each asatizah would also be required to renew their registration every three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: All ARS-asatizahs are also required to go for regular training, and their suitability is periodically reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: If there are reports or if they demonstrate that they are unfit to be asatizahs, such as breaching the Code of Ethics, their ARS status will be cancelled.

sections.label: ARS compulsory and registered asatizahs
sections.summary: ARS was made compulsory in 2017 and more than 4,000 asatizahs are currently registered under the scheme.
